threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid eye contact with the buskers on Kingsland Road, like they’re a wild animal you’re scared of.
Heard a bloke on the 12 bus at 2 AM arguing with a pigeon over a chip. The bird was winning. Peckham nightlife really is something else.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street performer juggling flaming torches next to a baby stroller on Karl-Marx-Straße. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Kebab place that stays open all night, serving fresh döner to the club crowds while the U-Bahn is on strike.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're from here when they react to the BART delays with a resigned shrug instead of panic. It’s the city’s soundtrack.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just watched a guy serenade a sleeping bus rider with a ukulele at Civic Center. Classic Muni moment—only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think La Rambla is the heart of Barcelona, but Gràcia’s narrow streets and local festes are where the real pulse of the city beats.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with their T-10 card, staring at the machines like they owe them money.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid the post-pub kebab shop on Kingsland Road like it's a tourist trap, while the rest of us know it's a rite of passage.
Saw a guy on the 59 last night trying to sell dodgy knock-off phone cases. The bus driver just rolled his eyes and kept driving.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy in a bunny costume handing out flyers for a vegan café while a street musician played Beethoven on a saxophone. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know that feeling when your U-Bahn route suddenly changes, and you have to follow the crowds exiting for a surprise street festival? Classic Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they casually know the Muni schedule by heart but still carry a backup plan for BART's inevitable breakdowns.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy serenading passengers on a delayed 38 bus with a ukulele, seemingly unfazed by the chaos around him. Classic San Francisco moment!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the tapas here are authentic; they miss the tiny, family-run spots that serve the real deal, hidden in the back alleys.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their confusion over how to order a café. It's always 'con leche' or just 'negro'—never just 'coffee'!
